links.outcome: Blinded physician ratings of LLM versus clinician responses across 11 quality domains
links.effect: Clinician mean ratings were lower than LLMs in 9/11 domains, e.g. guideline alignment 2.86 vs 4.25-4.72; expert knowledge 2.76 vs 4.25-4.73; harm extent 3.16 vs 4.29-4.68.
links.quote: Clinician mean ratings were lower than those for LLMs in 9/11 domains: 2.86 vs 4.25-4.72 (guideline alignment), 2.76 vs 4.25-4.73 (expert knowledge), 2.96 vs 4.30-4.73 (logical coherence), and 2.58 vs 4.16-4.68 (low omission of critical information).

links.outcome: Rated avoidance of demographic and socio-economic bias in LLM responses versus clinicians
links.effect: Avoidance of demographic bias rated 4.86 for clinicians vs 4.91-4.94 for LLMs; clinicians and LLMs similar, LLMs had >90% probability of high rating.
links.quote: Performance was similar for low inclusion of irrelevant content (4.28 vs 4.25-4.35) and for avoidance of demographic bias (4.86 vs 4.91-4.94).

unlisted_practices: Locally co-designed clinical vignettes from Kenyan primary care for benchmarking LLMs
Cost comparison of LLM-generated versus clinician-generated responses

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the clinical reasoning and response safety of multiple LLMs against local clinicians using primary care clinical vignettes in Kenya.
